scoring_justification: Full recompute from raw artifacts not feasible because only derived diffusion/planarity CSV provided; no raw MSD/trajectories included in output contract. Therefore compare reported values to paper-derived thresholds (D low at T≤800 K, D high at T≥1000 K; planarity high at T≤1000 K, low at T≥1100 K) with monotonic trend checks.

hidden_assets.purpose: Paper-derived acceptable ranges for diffusion coefficient and planarity ratio at various temperatures.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper text: 'melting starts above 900 K', diffusion coefficients from MSD plots are very low at 300-800 K and rise above 0.01 Å²/ps at 1000-1400 K; nanofilms stable up to 1000 K (planarity ratio high) and collapse above 1100 K (ratio < 2.0). Quantitative thresholds derived by combining paper description with typical simulation values.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Upper/lower bounds set with generous margins to accommodate different implementations while ensuring the expected physical regime is reproduced. The reference solver writes specific numbers that satisfy these bounds exactly.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Thresholds are grounded in the paper’s qualitative conclusions (low D at low T, high D above melting onset; planarity collapse above 1000 K) and match the regime of the reference solve.sh values, which are themselves plausible MD simulation results.

outputs.description: Diffusion coefficients for the four nanowire assemblies (5x55, 10x55, 5x147, 10x147) at each temperature. Melting onset is indicated when D exceeds a system-dependent threshold.

Planarity ratio (in-plane diameter / thickness) for the two nanofilm assemblies (5x5 of 55-atom clusters, 5x5 of 147-atom clusters) at each temperature. A ratio >= 2.0 indicates a stable film morphology.

output_contract.notes: The agent must run the full MD pipeline; the checker compares the reported D and planarity ratio values against hidden paper-derived thresholds, using threshold_or_better policy. No exact gold values are given in the public contract.
